title: Foreign Minister Lin leads delegation to Poland, further promoting and deepening ties with Europe and Poland
text:
Minister of Foreign Affairs Lin Chia-lung led a delegation to Poland from October 10 to 14. During the visit, he delivered a keynote speech at the Warsaw Security Forum and announced the signing of two MOUs—one concerning a technology park to be developed by the Taiwan Electrical and Electronic Manufacturers’ Association; the other relating to a cooperative initiative to boost semiconductor resilience. He also met with friends of Taiwan and high-level officials from a number of countries, including former acting president of Poland and Chair of the Polish Senate Foreign Affairs Committee Grzegorz Schetyna, Polish-Taiwanese Parliamentary Group Chair Krzysztof Truskolaski, former Lithuanian Minister of National Defense Dovilė Šakalienė, Czech MEP Markéta Gregorová, Chair of the Estonian Riigikogu Foreign Affairs Committee Marko Mihkelson, and other parliamentarians friendly to Taiwan. Minister Lin further visited Taiwanese businesses as well as organizations cooperating with Taiwan to provide humanitarian assistance in Ukraine. His trip showed Taiwan to be one of Europe’s most trusted democratic partners and did much to substantively deepen ties with Europe and Poland.

During his time in Poland, Minister Lin called at the Łukasiewicz Research Network’s Institute of Microelectronics and Photonics (ŁRN-IMiF) to announce the launch of a bilateral cooperation project on gallium nitride chip technology—the first Taiwan-Poland initiative to focus on semiconductor resilience. The project will be jointly administered by Taiwan’s Industrial Technology Research Institute and the ŁRN-IMiF after the two sides’ representative offices sign an MOU. Combining the research capabilities and industrial resources of both nations, the program will facilitate the development of a mutually beneficial industrial cycle under which Poland will transform Taiwan’s technology into practical applications that stimulate manufacturing demand back in Taiwan. This will allow both nations to bolster power semiconductor technology and explore new opportunities in power-intensive fields like electric vehicles and the energy sector.

Minister Lin also paid a special visit to Acer’s factory in Wrocław. Employing 400 personnel, the 20,000-square-meter facility serves as a key link in Acer’s European supply chain, as well as an important repair and service center. Through his time at the site, Minister Lin gained a deeper understanding of how Taiwanese businesses are using Poland as a gateway to Europe and discussed the shape of their investments in Poland.

Minister Lin’s itinerary also saw him visit the Polish Center for International Aid Foundation (PCPM), which serves as Taiwan’s local partner in cooperating with Poland to assist Ukraine. Reiterating that Taiwan would maintain its stanch support for Ukraine, Minister Lin said he hoped that Taiwan and the PCPM would continue to promote humanitarian assistance programs and contribute to Ukraine’s postwar rebuilding.

In addition, Minister Lin met for afternoon tea with two Ukrainian journalists, both of whom work for Poland’s national radio broadcaster and had previously visited Taiwan for short-term research and training. Minister Lin used the meeting to share the outcomes of Taiwan’s efforts to assist Ukraine. Both sides also said they looked forward to Taiwan, Poland, Ukraine, and other democratic partners engaging in cooperation and exchanges to jointly strengthen freedom of the press, boost societal resilience, and counter disinformation.

In pursuing its policy of integrated diplomacy, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MOFA) will promote a combination of values-based, alliance, and economic diplomacy as it works with like-minded European partners to advance collaborative, mutually beneficial initiatives. MOFA will continue to enhance economic, trade, and technological exchanges between Taiwan and Europe, foster mutual prosperity and security, and build on the foundations of values-based diplomacy to engage in value-added diplomacy. (E)
